description: This District of Columbia layer holds a condition assessment of sidewalks as line segments, each with a sidewalk condition index (SCI) from 0 to 11 where higher is better, and a category of excellent, good, fair, poor or failed. Fields also count the eight most common defects on each segment (minor cracking, serious cracking, separation, missing panels, settlement, patches, scaling and tree-root damage), give sidewalk length in feet, ownership, maintenance priority and the primary and secondary material. Coverage: Washington DC; the MapServer layer returned 24,577 segments on 2026-09-26. Access: free ArcGIS service and downloads through Open Data DC and data.gov (issued July 2024, item modified 2026-09-26). Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. Caveats: the survey date of each segment is not stated in the item description, and the scoring method is DDOT's own. Simulation uses: prioritising sidewalk repair, pedestrian accessibility routing and trip-hazard risk, and linking tree-root damage to street tree data. Related records: the Arlington County sidewalk inventory, Project Sidewalk accessibility labels and the NYC street tree census.
